issues.issue: Is the application moot, given the three-year TRPs and work permits?
issues.applicant_position: TRPs are temporary and revocable, so a live controversy remains; the RAD decision should be set aside and heard.
issues.respondent_position: TRPs make any risk speculative; an H&C application, not a s 97 claim, is the proper forum; the application is moot.
issues.result_quote: As such, the Court finds that the issues before it have become moot.

issues.issue: Did the RAD breach procedural fairness by deciding an unargued issue without notice?
issues.applicant_position: RAD raised and decided an unargued issue (independent claim, family separation) without notice or a chance to lead evidence.
issues.result_quote: The Court is in agreement with the Applicants that the RAD breached procedural fairness

issues.issue: Did the RAD unreasonably assume the applicants would leave their daughter in Canada and return to Nigeria?
issues.applicant_position: Returning without their daughter, who needs treatment, would be cruel and unusual treatment and would endanger her care.
issues.respondent_position: Any risk from eventual separation from the daughter is purely speculative, given the three-year TRPs.
issues.result_quote: As the preliminary question of mootness warrants the dismissal of this application, my analysis will limit itself to this first issue.

issues.issue: Did the RAD contravene the principle of non-refoulement?
issues.applicant_position: Returning the parents to Nigeria while the daughter stays in Canada for treatment contravened non-refoulement.
issues.result_quote: As the preliminary question of mootness warrants the dismissal of this application, my analysis will limit itself to this first issue.
